evidence: The health benefits of sun exposure arise from two distinct, interconnected mechanisms: (a) cutaneous synthesis of Vitamin D and (b) non-Vitamin D pathways (e.g., nitric oxide release, circadian regulation, psychological restoration).

Vitamin D2 (Ergocalciferol) ... Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol) ... Preferred form – it raises 25(OH)D levels 2–3x more effectively and maintains levels longer.
The evidence is clear: moderate, regular sun exposure and adequate Vitamin D are essential for health, but they are not interchangeable.

Outdoor exposure (≥1 hour/day) reduces the risk of myopia (nearsightedness) by 23% (Jones et al., Ophthalmology, 2022). This is a Vitamin D-independent effect.
Outdoor exposure (even without exercise) reduces all-cause mortality by 20% (Lindqvist et al., Journal of Internal Medicine, 2023). This is independent of Vitamin D levels.
Vitamin D supplementation reduces the risk of falls by 30% (via improved muscle strength and balance) (Bischoff-Ferrari et al., NEJM, 2022).
All statistics are derived from peer-reviewed studies published between 2020–2023.

The health benefits of sun exposure arise from two distinct, interconnected mechanisms: (a) cutaneous synthesis of Vitamin D and (b) non-Vitamin D pathways (e.g., nitric oxide release, circadian regulation, psychological restoration).

Rickets (children) / Osteomalacia (adults): Softening of bones.
Osteoporosis: Increased fracture risk.
